classification.difficultyReason: Several linked decisions using the demonstrated definitions or procedures. The union and intersection definitions show that equality occurs when there are no elements exclusive to either set.

content.prompt: Is it possible for $A\cap B$ to be equal to $A\cup B$?

answer.worked: Yes. When $A=B$, both the intersection and union equal $A$. Conversely, if the intersection equals the union, no element can belong to only one set, so $A=B$.
